scenarios.title: Sudden crash
scenarios.expectation: Equities fall 9% in a day and their intervals double: the LLM reduces risk (invested share at least 2 points below the baseline).

runs.analysis: The market is in a sharp risk-off phase: over the last 20 sessions SPY is down 17.4%, QQQ 21.4%, and NVDA 45.9%, with annualised volatility elevated across the board (SPY 51%, QQQ 63%, NVDA 95%). Forecast medians are all near zero (no directional edge), but the 80% interval widths are reliable risk signals: TLT remains the tightest (5d width 4.1%) and the only asset with positive recent returns, while QQQ (31.7%), EEM (32.8%) and NVDA (75.5%) carry the widest tails. The portfolio is in a -4% drawdown with only an 'alert' flag, so I am not forced to de-risk, but the breadth of the selloff justifies raising cash from the 10% minimum to ~18%. I fund this by cutting the two highest-uncertainty equity ETFs (QQQ and EEM) to zero and trimming XLE by 2pp (energy has a slightly negative median forecast and a -20.6% 20-day return). This keeps TLT at 24% as the defensive anchor, preserves the low-volatility health and financial sleeves, and limits changes to three assets so the proposal stays well inside the correction guardrails.

Market regime is clearly risk-off: every equity asset is down 10-46% over the past 20 sessions (SPY -17.4%, QQQ -21.4%, EEM -21.0%, NVDA -45.9%), while only TLT is positive (+0.6% 20d). The portfolio is in a -4% drawdown with 'alert' status, so no reduce-only restriction applies, but capital preservation is prudent. Forecast intervals confirm elevated uncertainty: 5-day q90-q10 widths range from 4% (TLT) to 75% (NVDA), with broad equity ETFs at 25-33%. Since median forecasts show no directional skill, I rely on interval width as the risk signal. The baseline already underweights high-uncertainty assets, but I can improve the risk profile by rotating out of the three highest-uncertainty broad exposures (EEM 33%, QQQ 32%, SPY 25% 5d width) and into the lowest-uncertainty equity sector (XLV health, 14% width) plus additional cash. Trades smaller than 2pp are not executed, so I use 2pp increments: cut SPY, QQQ, EEM by 2pp each, add 2pp to XLV, and raise cash from 10% to 14%. This lowers portfolio volatility, keeps group and asset caps intact, and leaves dry powder for re-entry if the selloff stabilizes. NVDA's extreme uncertainty (75% width) is noted, but its 1.29% weight is below the 2pp trade threshold, so it remains at baseline.

scenarios.title: One very uncertain asset
scenarios.expectation: NVDA's forecast interval is four times wider: the LLM does not pile into it.

runs.detail: NVDA +0.0 pts against its (already small) baseline
runs.analysis: The market is in a broad risk-off regime: over the last 20 sessions every equity asset is down (SPY -9.2%, QQQ -13.6%, EEM -13.2%, NVDA -40.5%), while long-duration Treasuries (TLT) are up +0.6% and have the narrowest forecast interval (width 4.1% over 5d), i.e. the highest confidence of a small, contained move. Forecast medians are all near zero, so there is no directional edge to chase; the reliable signal is the interval width, which is extremely wide for NVDA (151%), QQQ (15.9%), EEM (16.4%) and AMZN (14.0%), and narrow for TLT, XLV, XLF and IWM. I therefore rotate defensively: raise cash from 10% to 16.8% to preserve dry powder, increase TLT to 20% as the primary hedge, add to health care (XLV +2pp, LLY +2pp) which has shown relative resilience (XLV -1.1% 20d, LLY +5.9% 20d), and cut 2pp each from the weakest / highest-uncertainty exposures (SPY, QQQ, EFA, EEM, XLF, GLD, JPM, AMZN). NVDA stays at its tiny baseline because the 0.4pp reduction would not be traded and the interval is too wide to justify any size. All group caps, ETF/stock caps and the +15pp increase limit are respected; the portfolio remains long-only with 16.8% cash.

runs.detail: NVDA +0.0 pts against its (already small) baseline
runs.analysis: The market is in a clear risk-off regime: broad equities have sold off sharply (SPY -9.2% and QQQ -13.6% over 20d, NVDA -40%), while long-term Treasuries (TLT) have rallied (+2.6% 5d) and exhibit the lowest forecast uncertainty (5d interval width 0.041). scenarios.title: Drawdown: reduce-only mode
scenarios.expectation: The portfolio is 6% below its peak: the LLM proposes no increase at all.

runs.analysis: Market regime is clearly risk-off: over the last 20 sessions nearly every asset is down 6-13%, with tech growth (QQQ -13.6%, NVDA -40.5%) and emerging markets (EEM -13.2%) hit hardest. Only TLT is positive (+0.6% 20d). The portfolio is in a -6% drawdown and the 'reduce_only' action is active, so no position may be increased above its current weight; I can only trim risk and raise cash. Forecast medians are all near zero (no directional edge), but interval widths differ sharply: TLT (0.041), XLV (0.068) and XLF (0.072) have the narrowest 5-day intervals (lowest uncertainty), while NVDA (0.378), EEM (0.164) and QQQ (0.159) have the widest (highest uncertainty). Given the drawdown and reduce_only constraint, I cut the three assets that combine the steepest recent losses with the widest forecast uncertainty: QQQ, EEM and GLD, each by 2 percentage points. This moves 6 points to cash (cash rises from 10% to ~16%), lowering portfolio tail risk while keeping the defensive, low-uncertainty holdings (TLT, XLV, XLF) intact. NVDA is left unchanged because its 1.57% weight is too small to trade effectively (a change under 2 points would not execute). All group, asset-class and cash limits remain satisfied.

The portfolio is in a 6% drawdown with 'reduce_only' active, so no position may be increased above its current weight — my proposal therefore only reduces positions and raises cash. Market data shows a broad risk-off regime: over 20 days every equity asset is down (QQQ -13.6%, EEM -13.2%, NVDA -40.5%, GLD -11.9%), while only TLT (+0.6%) and LLY (+5.9%) are positive. The forecast intervals confirm where the risk sits: NVDA (5d width 37.8%), EEM (16.4%), QQQ (15.9%), AMZN (14.0%), SPY (12.6%) and GLD (11.9%) carry the widest 80% intervals, while TLT (4.1%), XLV (6.8%) and XLF (7.2%) are the most stable. Since the median has no directional skill, I am not cutting based on expected return but on interval width and the drawdown protocol: I cut the widest-interval assets hardest (GLD, AMZN, EEM, NVDA), trim the rest modestly, keep TLT/XLV/XLF as the defensive core, and raise cash from 10% to 16.4%. All 15 targets are strictly below current weights (satisfying reduce_only with margin), every group stays under 30%, ETFs under 25%, stocks under 10%, cash >= 10%, and the weights sum to exactly 1.0.

scenarios.title: Drawdown: exposure cap
scenarios.expectation: The portfolio is 9% below its peak: the LLM stays within the 60% exposure cap.

runs.analysis: Market regime is broad risk-off: the portfolio is 9% below peak, which triggers the drawdown actions 'reduce_only' and 'cap_exposure_60'. That means no position may be increased above its current weight and total invested must be <= 60% (cash >= 40%). The data confirm a selloff: every equity ETF and stock is negative over 1d/5d/20d except TLT (+0.6% 20d, +2.6% 5d) and LLY (+5.9% 20d); NVDA is -40% over 20d, QQQ -13.6%, EEM -13.2%, XLE/XOM/GLD around -12%. Since forecast medians have no directional skill, I lean on interval width (the reliable risk signal) plus recent momentum. Plan: raise cash from 10% to 43.36% and cut invested exposure from 90% to 56.64%. I keep the lowest-uncertainty, most defensive assets: TLT (narrowest interval of all, 0.041 5d, only positive momentum, low vol), XLV (narrowest equity interval 0.068, -1.1% 20d), XLF (0.072, -2.4% 20d), IWM (0.097, -6.9% 20d), EFA (0.105, intl diversification), JPM (0.104) and LLY (0.105, the only stock with positive 20d momentum). I trim SPY to 2% (wide interval 0.126, -9.2% 20d) to retain a token large-cap sleeve. I cut to zero the widest-interval and weakest-momentum names: NVDA (width 0.378, -40% 20d, vol 69%), EEM (0.164, -13.2%), QQQ (0.159, -13.6%, vol 40%), AMZN (0.140, vol 44%), GLD (0.119, -11.9% — gold is not acting as a hedge in this data), XLE (negative median both horizons, -12.7%) and XOM (-12.1%). Note: NVDA's cut is 1.57pp (<2pp, may not execute); even if it stays, invested is 58.2% <= 60%, so the cap holds either way. All group caps are respected (health 14.3%, financials 14.0%, us_broad 8.1%, bonds 14.6%), every target is <= current weight (reduce_only), and the proposal sums to 1 with cash 43.36% >= 10%.

Market is in a broad risk-off regime: every equity asset is down over 1d/5d/20d except TLT (+2.6% 5d). The portfolio is in a -9% drawdown, which triggers 'reduce_only' (cannot increase any position above current weight) and 'cap_exposure_60' (at most 60% invested, so cash >= 40%). Current exposure is 90%, so I must cut at least 30% to cash. Strategy: eliminate the highest-uncertainty and worst-drawdown assets first (NVDA: 38% 5d forecast width and -40% 20d; GLD: -12% 20d with wide interval), heavily reduce cyclical/tech/growth exposure (QQQ, EEM, AMZN, SPY), and preserve the defensive ballast (TLT at 14.61% — the only asset with positive recent returns and a narrow 4% interval; XLV at 8.67% — lowest volatility and smallest 20d drawdown). This brings invested capital to 54.78% and cash to 45.22%, satisfying the 60% cap while keeping dry powder for re-entry.

scenarios.title: Nothing happens
scenarios.expectation: Calm markets, portfolio at the baseline: the LLM stays close to it (at most 5 points moved), staying put being a legitimate decision.

runs.detail: 6.0 pts moved away from the baseline
runs.analysis: Regime read: this is a clear risk-off tape. Over the last 20 sessions SPY is -9.2%, QQQ -13.6%, EEM -13.2%, NVDA -40.5%, GLD -11.9% and energy ~-12%, while TLT is the only asset with positive momentum (+1.4% 1d, +2.6% 5d, +0.6% 20d) — a flight-to-quality into long Treasuries. Forecast medians are all near zero (no directional skill, as expected), so I act on interval widths (reliable risk info) and cross-asset behavior, not on medians. TLT has by far the narrowest 80% interval (5d width 0.041 vs 0.09-0.38 for everything else), making it the model's lowest-uncertainty asset exactly when equities are wobbling; long-duration bonds are the natural hedge here. The widest intervals plus worst momentum sit in QQQ (5d width 0.159, -13.6% 20d), EEM (0.164, -13.2%) and GLD (0.119, -11.9% — gold is falling with risk assets, not hedging). NVDA is the extreme case (width 0.378, -40% 20d, 69% vol) but is already at its minimal 1.6% baseline weight; cutting it further is below the 2pp trading threshold, so I leave it. Action: shift 6pp in 2pp slices from QQQ, EEM and GLD into TLT (14.6% -> 20.6%, under the 25% ETF cap and within the +15pp increase limit), cash held at the 10% minimum. Risk-asset exposure falls from ~70% to ~64% with bonds at ~20.6%. Drawdown is 0, so no forced de-risking applies. Main risk to the tilt: a sharp mean-reversion rally in equities, which this positioning would lag; given zero median skill I prefer the lower-uncertainty allocation.

runs.detail: 9.4 pts moved away from the baseline

Forecast intervals confirm elevated uncertainty in growth and emerging assets (NVDA width 0.38, EEM 0.16, QQQ 0.16) versus very low uncertainty in bonds (TLT 0.04) and defensive healthcare (XLV 0.07). scenarios.title: A tempting median
scenarios.expectation: Only the median of AMZN's forecast moves (+8%), not its uncertainty: the LLM does not chase it, the prompt says the median has no measured skill.

runs.detail: AMZN +3.8 pts although only its median moved (+8%)
runs.analysis: Regime read: broad risk-off. Over the last 20 sessions every equity asset is down (SPY -9.2%, QQQ -13.6%, EEM -13.2%, XLE -12.7%, NVDA -40%, GLD -11.9%); the only positive 20d performer is TLT (+0.6%, +2.6% over 5d). Forecast medians are all near zero (no directional skill), so decisions rest on interval width and cross-asset structure. Three data-driven signals stand out: (1) TLT has by far the narrowest 80% intervals (1.9% 1d / 4.1% 5d) and the only positive recent momentum — the natural defensive anchor; (2) NVDA has the widest interval by a huge margin (37.8% 5d) with 69% annualized vol and a -40% 20d drawdown — single-name tail risk worth eliminating; (3) AMZN is the only asset whose entire 80% forecast interval is above zero on both horizons (1d q10 +4.7%, 5d q10 +1.0%) while being the most resilient equity over 20d (-0.5% vs QQQ -13.6%) — a modest overweight is justified, kept below the 10% single-stock cap. Plan: raise cash 10%→15% for dry powder, lift TLT 14.6%→20% (within +15pp of baseline and the 25% ETF cap), lift AMZN 4.2%→8%, cut NVDA to 0, and fund this by trimming ~2pp each from SPY, QQQ, EEM, XLE, XOM and GLD — the assets with the widest intervals and/or worst 20d momentum. Keep IWM (narrowest equity interval, 9.7%), XLV/XLF (narrow intervals, defensive sectors), EFA, JPM and LLY at baseline (LLY is the only equity with a positive 20d return). Resulting equity exposure falls from ~75% to ~65% invested, cash 15% ≥ 10% minimum, all group caps respected (tech_growth 9.7%, us_broad 8.8%, energy 8.5%, health 14.3%, financials 14.0%), all increases within +15pp of baseline. Main risk: after a sharp selloff, mean reversion could favor the trimmed equities; I accept that, sizing the defensive shift moderately rather than maximally. Overall confidence in the deviation beating the baseline risk-adjusted over 5 days: ~0.55.

runs.detail: AMZN +3.8 pts although only its median moved (+8%)
runs.analysis: Market regime is risk-off: broad equity indices are down 7-13% over 20 days (SPY -9.2%, QQQ -13.6%, EEM -13.2%, NVDA -40.5%) with only TLT (+0.6% 20d) and XLV (-1.1% 20d) holding up, indicating a flight to safety. Forecast intervals confirm elevated uncertainty in tech and emerging markets (5-day widths of 15.9% for QQQ, 16.4% for EEM, 37.8% for NVDA) while defensive assets (TLT 4.1%, XLV 6.8%, XLF 7.2%) show narrow intervals. Notably, AMZN is the only asset with a positive q10 forecast (+1.01% 5d, +4.71% 1d), meaning the model assigns less than 10% probability to a negative cumulative return over the horizon—a strong downside-protection signal despite the recent -4.1% daily drop. I am tilting toward AMZN (to 8.0%) funded by eliminating NVDA (extreme volatility, severe drawdown), cutting QQQ and EEM by ~2pp each, and trimming GLD (redundant with TLT ballast). Cash is raised to 14.6% to preserve dry powder amid the broad sell-off. Defensive anchors TLT (14.6%) and XLV (8.7%) are maintained at baseline given their low forecast uncertainty and relative resilience. All group limits (tech_growth 9.5%, energy 12.5%, health 14.3%, financials 14.0%) remain well below the 30% cap.
